dogecoin.text: That's how it should work. Someone (anyone) releases code and the community adopts/rejects it based on experience with the team, the case made for/against the update, etc.

If we wrote a client that forked to give us billions of Doge, you'd tell us to get knotted, right? So it wouldn't ever get through.

If we add in sidechain functionality for Doge/Eth tokens, you'll probably accept it.

However, we have to negotiate with EVERYONE for this.

Reminded, I was reading https://t.co/QbJG2bIaSq

The whole thing where the exchange tries to sue the developers for not hard forking is insane.

You want a hard fork, you write the code and release it. That's it. We're not the gatekeepers, the community is.

This is important because single points of failure are what cryptocurrency is meant to defend against. If @dogecoin was ever hacked, heaven forbid, I'd want to know you guys would realise it was talking nonsense and make good decisions.
The Doge/Eth bridge work is being done by an entirely independent team, who are even funded via Eth rather than Doge. We have status meetings from time to time, but neither of us leads the other.

@Bitcoin Dogecoin for example has multiple different teams doing different things. Max, Patrick & myself working Dogecoin Core. The reddit mods are an independent team we get along well with, but we have to negotiate changes with them.

The @bitcoin account has been suspended again, but...

Listen, I was serious about the decentralised bit. If cryptocurrencies are run by a central "trusted" party, they're just an inefficient reinvention of existing payments
@ComradeEevee @MSingularity For the main https://t.co/ZPhL6cDSCC site there's a bunch of politics to negotiate, rather than concerns about what you might do. Lets see what Movable says :)
@Muhamma38785734 @Bitcoin Oh they've suspended the account again. It looks like the account was suspended, then deleted, then someone random managed to register it.
@ComradeEevee @MSingularity What's the political situation with the main website? Or, is it going to be easier for me to just give @ComradeEevee one of the other domains and let them run wild?

Cryptocurrency is of course intended to be decentralised, and you should look to no single party as authoritative.

In related news, some random guy in Turkey is now in control of @bitcoin.
